review.title: Unknown media metadata semantics
review.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contained PL-0706's single leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, and pathsOverlap tests containment in both directions, so a package-wide reservation for a five-file change held the whole media lane behind one security corrective. The five entries were read out of the implementation, not guessed: shared/media-facts.ts declares the MediaFact vocabulary and MEDIA_FACTS canonical order and exists only for this task; shared/codecs.ts carries the named VideoCodec and AudioCodec types this task introduced; domains/playback.ts holds the required-and-nullable candidate fields, unknownMediaFacts and compatibilityConfidenceSchema under a header naming PL-0201 and this task; stream-candidate.test.ts and stream-candidate.property.test.ts are its regressions; and testing/arbitraries.ts carries mediaFactsArb, UNKNOWN_FACT_FREQ, statedMediaFactsArb and statedStreamCandidateArb. All are prefix-disjoint from packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts in both directions. testing/arbitraries.ts is shared with PL-0204 on purpose and both surfaces are stated honestly rather than one being trimmed to avoid the overlap; see that task's note for what the overlap does and does not cost, and note that it costs nothing extra here because packages/media-engine/** already makes these three tasks mutually exclusive. packages/contracts/src/index.ts is deliberately NOT declared: it is a re-export-only barrel with an export * line already covering shared/ and domains/, so nothing this task did required editing it, and declaring an untouched file pads a review range exactly as omitting a touched one narrows it.
review.acceptance: StreamCandidate can represent genuinely unknown videoCodec, audioCodec, height and bitrateKbps, and the media engine treats unknown as unknown rather than as a value: eligibility must not pass on an unverified codec, and scoring must not award or penalise a fabricated number

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck via npm run check, exit 0 under pinned Node 22 on the tree committed this round. The four facts are required-and-nullable rather than optional, so unknown must be asserted and cannot be reached by silence, and CODEC_EFFICIENCY is keyed by VideoCodec rather than by the candidate field precisely so a null cannot index it.

unit.evidence: vitest via npm run check, exit 0 on the tree committed this round. packages/contracts/src/stream-candidate.test.ts and its property sibling pin that an explicit null parses while an omitted or undefined fact is rejected and a numeric sentinel is refused; packages/media-engine/src/unknown-media.test.ts and unknown-vs-known.property.test.ts pin that an unstated codec is neither rejected nor certified, that a stated codec the device cannot decode is still rejected, that a height nobody stated cannot exceed maxHeight, that rights are checked before anything unknown can excuse a candidate, and that every unknowable dimension scores zero on a positive weight with no renormalisation, so a fabricated number is neither awarded nor penalised. ONE READING TO SETTLE, RAISED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the acceptance says eligibility must not PASS on an unverified codec, and the implementation reads that as must not CERTIFY -- an unstated codec is admitted as attemptable and labelled unverified rather than rejected, and ranking.ts argues that reading explicitly on the ground that rejecting it would report a device limitation nobody has demonstrated. If the reviewer reads the clause the other way, the acceptance is what is wrong and not the code.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The implementation predates the claim: packages/contracts/src/shared/media-facts.ts, the MediaFact vocabulary that exists only for this task, plus the required-and-nullable candidate fields in domains/playback.ts and the unknown-aware scoring and ranking in packages/media-engine, are all already in committed history under headers naming PL-0205, while the task itself was never claimed and carried no gate results. The base is DERIVED, not chosen: the first commit reported by git rev-list --reverse HEAD -- packages/contracts/src/shared/media-facts.ts is the commit that created that file, and this base is its first parent, resolved with rev-parse --verify so a root commit with no parent aborts the reconcile rather than silently widening it. That file is the narrowest probe available because nothing else in the repository would have created it. Nothing here shrinks a range or pads one; the window, both endpoints and the changed-file count are published for the reviewer to judge, because git does not attribute commits to tasks and no mechanism can.

review.title: Catalog metadata source port, and the surfaces still importing the fixture array
review.notes: Closes a control-plane gap as well as a code one. The port landed with no task covering it: PL-0104 declares only catalog-card.tsx, routes.ts and routes.test.ts, so apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts, catalog-source-registry.ts, their tests and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md sat outside every declared surface - unreserved against a parallel writer, and outside any approval fingerprint. This task declares that surface and carries the three import migrations docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md lists as follow-ups. lib/catalog.ts and lib/demo-catalog.ts are reviewDependencies rather than allowedPaths: the port's wiring lives in them and an approval has to bind to it, but they are not this task's to rewrite. The e2e mode split that catalog.api.spec.ts needs once the fixtures stop reaching a production build is deliberately NOT here, because e2e/** belongs to PL-0701; until it lands, that spec fails in the harness's default production mode and .github/workflows/ci.yml says so at the job that runs it. DECLARATION GAP CLOSED: e2e/src/env.ts added to allowedPaths. It was edited this round and no task declared it as a write path -- it sat only in PL-0706's reviewDependencies, which is a READ-ONLY surface by contract, so the edit was a genuine contract violation and an approval on either task would have bound to a surface narrower than the diff. The edit is THIS task's, not PL-0706's: the rewritten CATALOG_AVAILABILITY commentary is entirely about the port and the import migrations named in this task's acceptance -- the title route now resolving through lib/catalog-source-registry.ts via resolveSynchronousCatalogMetadataSource so demo-title-details.ts classifies no environment, the four discovery surfaces refusing in the single catalog_source_not_configured vocabulary, and the deletion of readFixtureCatalogItems from catalog-source-registry.ts together with getHomeCatalog from lib/catalog.ts. Its only reference to the runtime witness is the unchanged phrase 'the same nominal witness the playback fixtures need', which was true before PL-0706's move and is true after it; nothing in this file names a class, a constructor or classifyRuntime. env.ts is deliberately LEFT in PL-0706's reviewDependencies rather than removed: WEB_MODE and MANAGES_SERVER decide that task's production-versus-development assertion, so its approval must keep fingerprinting this file even though it does not own it -- which is exactly what the two-surface split is for, and is not the same-task allowedPaths/reviewDependencies redundancy the validator warns on. Collision-checked: e2e/src/env.ts is prefix-disjoint from every allowedPaths entry of PL-0203 (claude-media), PL-AI-0005 (claude-lead) and PL-0706 (claude-security, whose e2e entries are e2e/tests/*.spec.ts and e2e/src/fixtures.ts), and PL-0104 shares this task's owner so cannot conflict. PL-0701 declares e2e/** but is BACKLOG and unowned, and already latently contains this task's apps/web paths and PL-0706's e2e specs, so nothing new is created there. REVIEW SURFACE WIDENED BY TWO FILES ON gpt-architect's THIRD-PASS FINDING, AND THE FINDING IS ABOUT PROVENANCE RATHER THAN CODE. The reviewer closed every implementation blocker on this task and then refused it anyway, because the acceptance sentence below claims the fixtures are UNCONSTRUCTIBLE IN A DEPLOYMENT while nothing in the declared surface establishes that: catalog-source-registry.ts depends on apps/web/src/app/api/deployment-environment.ts, whose authority in turn lives entirely in packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, and neither file was fingerprinted. An edit to either could have falsified this task's central guarantee while its approval stayed cryptographically fresh -- which is the same defect class PL-AI-0005 existed to remove, arriving here through a declaration rather than through the worker. Both are added as reviewDependencies and NOT as allowedPaths: this task does not write either, packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts is PL-0706's write surface and declaring it here would create an active write-path conflict between two owners, and reviewDependencies is precisely the read-only widening that exists for a boundary a task depends on but does not own. The immediate consequence is intended and was named by the reviewer: PL-0706's allowlist freeze lands in a file this task now fingerprints, so this approval cannot be granted against a tree that predates it, and any later change to the shared mint forces this rights review to be taken again rather than silently inheriting an answer given about a different mechanism.
review.acceptance: Discovery reads a metadata port instead of importing a fixture array. catalog-source.ts states the source contract in the published vocabulary - a CatalogItem plus a nullable rights basis - and refuses a record whose basis is undeclared or contradicts its item, by named reason, rather than defaulting either to something permissive; catalog-source-registry.ts is the only module that knows both the port and an implementation, and resolves to not-configured outside the NonDeploymentEnvironment allowlist so the fixtures are unconstructible in a deployment rather than withheld from one; and every remaining surface reads the registry rather than the demoCatalog array - app/search/search.ts, app/title/demo-title-details.ts, and app/api/v1/catalog/home/route.ts, which awaits loadHomeCatalog and maps catalog_source_not_configured onto its own status instead of serving empty rails at 200. When the last surface has moved, the raw demoCatalog export survives only for tests that must be able to name the fixture set, so search and the title page stop being fixture-backed on a build where the home rails are not. docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md stays accurate about what the port still does not solve.

review.title: Corrective, re-run: production rights-invariant breach in the watch route
review.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0703 and carries the same corrective forward under an honest review range. PL-0703 recorded implementationBaseSha f6c4b942ebbd02fd3fa9ed8f74fde4fc603affc2, which opened its review range AFTER part of the implementation already existed: the first incident repair at 9933a55 falls before that base and was therefore excluded from the range the first review was bound to. That record cannot be repaired in place. release is reachable only from CLAIMED or IN_PROGRESS and PL-0703 is in REVIEW; release deliberately PRESERVES implementationBaseSha even when it is usable; and reconciliation refuses any task that already records a base, because reconciliation establishes a base rather than revising one. The prescribed remedy is therefore to BLOCK PL-0703, preserving the false narrowed base as audit history, and to run the work again here. THIS TASK'S OWN BASE MUST BE RECONCILED, not captured: claim it, then start it with --reconcile-existing --base cf98b977b3c7c0113928bb9cc4d7fb6d02e802bd. That sha is the true pre-implementation base, being the immediate parent of the first incident-repair commit. Do NOT use its own parent b0b1dcf5a4826b763aa72d6375dd93e95a3aff33, which would widen the asserted range by one unrelated commit and make implementationBaseSha false in the other direction. The allowedPaths below are PL-0703's declared set plus packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/** and packages/provider-sdk/src/index.ts, because this round's corrective collapsed the two fixture providers onto the SDK's one and therefore writes there. The reviewDependencies carry over e2e/tests/media-rig.spec.ts and add e2e/src/env.ts and e2e/src/fixtures.ts: WEB_MODE and MANAGES_SERVER in the first decide the production-versus-development assertion, and TINY_DEVICE in the second is the probe that makes the unknown-height regression meaningful, so an approval that did not fingerprint them would stay artificially fresh after someone altered the mode classifier or the probe. packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/** is deliberately NOT also listed as a reviewDependency: it is a write path here, allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, and the validator warns on the redundancy.
review.notes: NOT ONLY A PROVENANCE REWRITE. At the previous head the reviewer refused BOTH security-review and rights-review ON THE MERITS, and those refusals are the substantive work this task inherits: the corrective had not reduced the fixture providers to one with the application consuming the SDK's, the runtime allowlist was not expressed exactly once with the SDK holding a witness it can neither forge nor classify for itself, the opaque rights-reference rule still existed in more than one place, a fabricated rights basis remained reachable behind a deletable condition rather than being structurally unconstructible in a deployment environment, and the two Playwright modes were not both shown as EXECUTED. PL-0703's typecheck, unit and e2e passes belong to that abandoned round and do not carry over; every gate here is re-recorded under this task's owner. ALLOWEDPATHS WIDENED BY EXACTLY ONE LEAF, packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, for the construction boundary the reviewer refused on. gpt-architect withheld security-review and rights-review in this round's review because the SDK's construction boundary is still forgeable: RuntimeClassification is a public STRUCTURAL interface carrying only nodeEnv, packages/provider-sdk/src/index.ts exports both it and createFixtureProvider, and createFixtureProvider mints its nominal NonProductionRuntime witness from whatever structural object it is handed -- so any caller can pass an object literal from a production process and obtain a real FixtureRightsBasis. fixture/environment.ts concedes the point in its own header: a literal satisfies it too. The prescription was a single NOMINAL runtime capability at a LOWER SHARED BOUNDARY that both the app and the SDK consume, with exactly one place performing the classification; a second duplicated allowlist and any weakening of this task's acceptance were both explicitly refused. No such boundary is reachable from the paths already declared here. apps/web/src/app/api/deployment-environment.ts is imported by five non-test modules under apps/web/src/lib/** that this task does not own -- session/account.ts, demo-catalog.ts, catalog-source-registry.ts, db/index.ts and db/in-memory-repository.ts -- so relocating it is not this task's to do; and routing the classification through @liberty/provider-sdk is worse, because that package publishes a single root entry point (exports is the bare string ./src/index.ts) and would drag the whole provider SDK into the module graph of every surface that renders a catalog card. @liberty/contracts is already a declared dependency of BOTH apps/web and packages/provider-sdk, and its exports map already carries a ./shared/* wildcard that apps/web, media-engine and recommendations import through today, so a new leaf module there needs no manifest, workspace, tsconfig or turbo change. Every path, edge and export named in this paragraph was read out of the tree rather than taken on report. The declaration is the single leaf file rather than packages/contracts/**, because that is the narrowest surface that admits the fix. SEQUENCING, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: PL-0203 declares packages/contracts/** and is still active, and pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in EITHER direction, so this leaf collides with PL-0203 exactly as the wide prefix would. ai:validate reports an active write-path conflict between PL-0203 and PL-0706 until PL-0203 leaves CLAIMED/IN_PROGRESS/REVIEW, so PL-0203's approval and completion have to land before this widening is validated. WIDENED A SECOND TIME, BY FOUR INDIVIDUAL FILES AND DELIBERATELY NOT BY apps/web/src/lib/**: a glob over that directory would contain PL-0105's own apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts and catalog-source-registry.ts and collide with an active task, whereas apps/web/src/lib/demo-catalog.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/index.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.ts and apps/web/src/lib/session/account.ts are prefix-disjoint from every path PL-0105 declares as a write surface; each of those four documents the environment gate in its header and none of them could keep describing it accurately once the allowlist and the capability moved out of apps/web into packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, and this repository treats a false comment as a defect, so correcting all four is part of this same change rather than follow-up -- which supersedes the sentence above stating the widening is exactly one leaf. DECLARATION GAP CLOSED, THIRD WIDENING, TWO FILES, AND ONE OF THEM IS A MOVE BETWEEN SURFACES. (1) e2e/src/fixtures.ts MOVED from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths. reviewDependencies is read-only by contract and this file was EDITED this round, so leaving it there was a real violation rather than a bookkeeping nicety: no collision check had reserved it, and the description's paragraph above -- which argues fixtures.ts belongs on the read-only surface for TINY_DEVICE -- was written before this round's edit and is superseded here rather than deleted. The edit is unmistakably this task's: the DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_HEADER commentary now states that NonDeploymentEnvironment 'is not a class and has no constructor of any kind: it is a branded value, minted only by classifyRuntime in @liberty/contracts/shared/runtime, whose brand key is a unique symbol that module never exports' -- it names the module this task created and explicitly retracts the private-constructor witness this task replaced. It is NOT also left as a reviewDependency, because allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface and the validator warns on that redundancy; the approval still fingerprints it. (2) docs/API_CONTRACTS.md added to allowedPaths: its storage-selection section was corrected to the same new fact, now reading that createInMemoryRepository requires the branded capability classifyRuntime issues in @liberty/contracts/shared/runtime, 'not a class, and with no constructor at all', with the allowlist 'declared there and nowhere else'. That is this task's correction of a claim this task falsified, and product invariant 5 makes the contracts doc part of the change rather than a follow-up. FUTURE COLLISION, RECORDED DELIBERATELY: PL-0601 also declares docs/API_CONTRACTS.md and is READY and unowned, so no active write-path conflict exists today and ai:validate is unaffected. It was declared here anyway because the alternative -- leaving a rights-relevant correction outside every declared surface -- is the exact defect this record exists to prevent, and because the collision it creates is not a new one: PL-0601 also declares packages/contracts/**, which already prefix-contains this task's packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and already overlaps PL-0203's and PL-0206's packages/contracts/**. PL-0601 is therefore already unclaimable while this task is active, and adding a second overlapping entry to an already-overlapping pair changes neither validate's verdict nor dispatch's. Sequence PL-0601 after this task and PL-0203, as the paragraph above already requires. NOT DECLARED, AND THE OMISSION IS THE FINDING: apps/web/src/lib/db/index.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts and apps/web/src/lib/session/account.test.ts were reported as changed by this round's runtime-capability move and were NOT. Each was read: none asserts a private constructor, none states where the allowlist lives, and none names classifyRuntime -- they speak of 'the witness' and 'the exported allowlist', wording that survived the move unaltered, which is precisely why app/api/deployment-environment.ts kept its re-export line and its NonDeploymentEnvironment.classify shape ('so the app's own suites can keep importing the set from the module they already import the classification from'). Their on-disk modification times sit in the earlier persistence-wiring round beside db/request-context.ts and db/reason-trail.ts, well before this round's cluster. Declaring an unchanged file would pad the review range as surely as omitting a changed one narrows it, so all three were declined. COLLISION-CHECKED BEFORE ADDING: e2e/src/fixtures.ts and docs/API_CONTRACTS.md are prefix-disjoint from every allowedPaths entry of the other active tasks -- PL-0104 and PL-0105 (claude-frontend), PL-0203 (claude-media), PL-AI-0005 (claude-lead) -- including PL-0105's newly declared sibling e2e/src/env.ts, which is neither a prefix of e2e/src/fixtures.ts nor contained by it, and PL-AI-0005's newly declared docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/GITHUB_SETUP.md. No second active conflict is created; the only one remains PL-0203 versus this task over packages/contracts. FOURTH WIDENING, SIX TEST FILES, AND IT SUPERSEDES THE DECLINE RECORDED ABOVE: this corrective took the environment-name parameter off the mint, so every suite that used to obtain a capability by naming an environment had to be rewritten to call the parameterless classify() and handle its null, and those rewrites are part of this change rather than follow-up -- apps/web/src/lib/db/index.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts, apps/web/src/lib/session/account.test.ts, apps/web/src/app/api/v1/profiles/handler.test.ts, apps/web/src/app/api/v1/watchlist/handler.test.ts and apps/web/src/app/api/v1/progress/handler.test.ts. Each was re-read before being declared: all six call NonDeploymentEnvironment.classify() with no argument and branch on the null, the first three narrate the removal in their own headers ('It used to pass a nodeEnv string, so one loop over a list of names could exercise both branches at once -- which was exactly the hole the corrective closed'), and the last three hand the resulting witness to createInMemoryRepository, which now takes it. Wording that could only have been written after the mint changed is direct evidence of an edit made after the paragraph above declined the first three as unchanged, so that decline is superseded on the facts rather than reversed on report; padding a review range is the same defect as narrowing one, and nothing is declared here without that evidence. COLLISION-CHECKED BEFORE ADDING: the active set is PL-AI-0005 (claude-lead), PL-0105 (claude-frontend) and this task (claude-security), and all six entries are prefix-disjoint in BOTH directions from every allowedPaths entry of the other two -- PL-0105's apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts and catalog-source-registry.ts and their tests, app/search/**, app/title/demo-title-details.ts, app/api/v1/catalog/home/**, docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md and e2e/src/env.ts contain none of them and are contained by none, and PL-AI-0005 declares only scripts paths and two docs. apps/web/** is declared by PL-0701 (BACKLOG) and PL-AI-0006 (READY), both unowned and both already prefix-containing this task's existing apps/web entries, so no new active conflict is created and validate's verdict is unchanged. Nor are the six redundant with this task's own db/index.ts, db/in-memory-repository.ts and session/account.ts: a .ts path is not a prefix of its .test.ts sibling. FOURTH REFUSAL OF THIS CONSTRUCTION BOUNDARY, AND THE DEFECT MOVED ONE INPUT FURTHER OUT AGAIN. Taking the argument off the mint was accepted as correct, and the reviewer then found that the authority had simply relocated into the array the argument-free mint consults: NON_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENTS was exported as readonly string[], which is a compile-time claim over an ordinary mutable array, so a consumer could cast it, append production, and then call the parameterless classifyRuntime() from a genuine production process and receive a genuine branded, frozen, identity-registered capability that every downstream check would correctly accept. The caller could no longer state the permission-granting fact, but it could still rewrite what the official classifier admits, without editing the classifier. The array is now frozen with Object.freeze, and because a module is always strict the attempted write throws rather than failing silently. ONE HARDENING BEYOND WHAT WAS ASKED, AND IT IS THE SAME HOLE FROM THE METHOD SIDE: isNonDeploymentEnvironmentName no longer calls Array.prototype.includes, which is a writable property of an object every module can reach -- a single assignment to it would have made the predicate answer true for production while the frozen array it was asked about remained correct. It walks the frozen array by index instead, so the only trusted operations are own-property reads on a frozen object. What remains is patching Object.freeze itself before this module loads, and that is named in the module header alongside the other statements-executing-inside-the-deployment rather than defended against, because any defence would be built out of the same built-ins. FIFTH WIDENING, ONE FILE: packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.test.ts, a new regression file. It pins the property rather than the implementation -- that nothing a consumer can execute may cause classifyRuntime() to admit a production process -- with the cast-and-append, the index overwrite, the length truncation, the prototype patch, and the end-to-end case that sets NODE_ENV=production, attempts the mutation and asserts the mint answers null, plus a positive case so a gate that refused everything could not pass the negative one for the wrong reason. Collision-checked: PL-0105 (claude-frontend) declares no packages path as a write surface, and the two contracts paths it gained this round are reviewDependencies, which reserve nothing. PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 declared packages/contracts/** and were narrowed this round precisely so they no longer prefix-contain this task's two contracts files; none of their narrowed entries is a prefix of either, in either direction. ACCEPTANCE CORRECTED RATHER THAN THE CODE MOVED, on the reviewer's explicit instruction: the sentence claiming the allowlist is expressed once BY THE APPLICATION and that the witness is APPLICATION-ISSUED was written before the boundary moved and now contradicts the architecture the reviewer required. It described the arrangement this task abandoned when the classification went into packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts as the lower shared boundary. It now records the final architecture -- one shared lower-boundary allowlist, frozen at runtime, a mint that observes the process with no caller-supplied name, the application obtaining the capability, the SDK able neither to classify nor to forge it. This is a provenance correction to the task contract; nothing about the implementation changed to satisfy it, which is the direction the reviewer specifically forbade. DEFERRED WIDENING RULED ON AND KEPT: the reviewer was asked directly whether hardening demoCatalogSource, selectRepository, createInMemoryRepository and developmentAccount against the registry, after it had deferred exactly that, was the wrong call. It answered yes, keep it, and keep it in this task rather than splitting it out, on the ground that leaving some permission-granting consumers on type-only validation would have produced two security meanings for the same capability.
review.acceptance: Exactly ONE fixture provider exists in the repository, and the application CONSUMES the provider-sdk's rather than implementing its own: no route, no API handler and no watch-surface module declares a rights basis, composes a media URL, invents a candidate id or carries its own copy of the fixture variants. The runtime allowlist that decides which environments may construct fixtures is expressed exactly ONCE, at a shared lower boundary both the application and the SDK depend on rather than in either of them, and it is frozen at runtime so no consumer can widen what the classifier admits without editing that module. The capability is minted there by observing the running process, with no caller-supplied runtime name anywhere on the path, so a caller can neither state the classification nor alter the set of classifications that are admissible. The application OBTAINS that capability and passes it on; the SDK can neither classify for itself nor forge what it is handed, and therefore cannot admit itself into a deployment. The opaque rights-reference rule exists in exactly ONE place, with every other consumer importing it rather than restating it. A fabricated rights basis is structurally UNCONSTRUCTIBLE in a deployment environment -- unreachable because nothing that constructs one can be reached without a capability the shared boundary mints from the running process, and a deployment cannot obtain one -- rather than guarded by a condition that deleting one line would remove. Both Playwright modes, production and development, are EXECUTED rather than only typechecked, and the gate evidence names the run, the commit and the per-mode results.

recommended.title: Candidate failover policy
recommended.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. This task declared packages/contracts/** for a change that touches exactly two files in that package. pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in BOTH directions, so that wildcard prefix-contained PL-0706's single leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and made this task unclaimable for as long as a security corrective held one forty-line file. It was not alone: PL-0205, PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 all declared the same wildcard, so one leaf starved four P0 tasks across two lanes while claude-media sat idle and ai:dispatch correctly returned an empty wave. A reservation is supposed to name what a task writes; a package-wide wildcard names what its package contains, and the difference is a whole lane. The two entries below were derived by reading the implementation rather than guessed: domains/failover.ts declares playbackFailureKindSchema, PLAYBACK_FAILURE_KINDS, playbackAttemptFailureSchema and failoverPolicySchema under a header naming this task, and testing/arbitraries.ts carries playbackFailureKindArb and failoverPolicyArb. Both are prefix-disjoint from packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts in both directions. testing/arbitraries.ts is ALSO declared by PL-0205, deliberately, and the overlap is real rather than an oversight: both tasks genuinely wrote that file, and declaring it on one of them alone would understate one review surface to flatter the other. Being precise about what that costs, because two different rules are easy to conflate here: ai:validate ERRORS only on an active write-path conflict under DIFFERENT owners, so this shared entry never makes validate fail while both tasks share claude-media -- but conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner. Combined with claude-media's maxParallel of 1, that means exactly one of PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 can be active at a time, and packages/media-engine/** would have forced that anyway. packages/media-engine/** is left wide on purpose -- this task, PL-0205 and PL-0206 all write across that package, they share an owner, and narrowing it would buy nothing. THE IMPLEMENTATION PREDATES THE CLAIM, AND THIS TASK IS QUEUED BEHIND PL-0205 RATHER THAN RECONCILED WITH IT. packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts, packages/media-engine/src/scheduling.ts and failover.ts, four test suites, a dedicated vitest config and a bench script are all already in committed history under headers naming this task, while it was never claimed and carries no gate results -- so ai:start must not capture HEAD here either; it needs --reconcile-existing with a base derived from git, the first parent of the first commit reported by git rev-list --reverse HEAD over packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts. That contract module is the right probe rather than a media-engine file, because the engine package already existed for PL-0201 and PL-0202 and its earliest touch would open the range two tasks too early. IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN THE SAME ROUND AS PL-0205 AND THE LIMIT IS MECHANICAL, NOT CAUTIOUS: claude-media declares maxParallel 1 in control/agents.json and ai:claim throws on it, and conflictWithActive refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner -- unlike ai:validate's error, which is scoped to different owners -- so packages/media-engine/** alone means exactly one of PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 can be active at a time whatever the capacity is set to. PL-0205 went first because this task rests on it: failover.ts opens by saying this is where the three-way distinction PL-0205 established stops being bookkeeping and starts deciding things, and reviewing a consumer before the vocabulary it consumes is backwards. ONE THING FOR WHOEVER RECONCILES THIS: the performance gate cannot be recorded from npm run check. The single wall-clock assertion in failover.perf.test.ts is deselected BY NAME in packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts unless vitest runs --mode bench, so a gate taken from the ordinary suite would describe the five deterministic read-count assertions and silently omit the timed one. Run npm run bench:failover in that workspace and record the gate from that, and only if it exits 0.

recommended.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
recommended.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
recommended.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.
